newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suspected militants kill two in south Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Suspected militants kill two in south Egypt.

text.p: Gunmen thought to be Islamist militants shot dead a doctor and a teacher in an attack on a clinic in southern Egypt on Saturday, security sources said. A farmer was shot and wounded.

The two gunmen burst into the clinic in the village of Qalaba in Minya province about 300 km (180 miles) south of Cairo after dark and killed the doctor, a Christian called Michel Ayad Hanna, 40, they said.
The teacher, 38-year-old Samir Mohamed Abdelkafi, tried to stop them as they escaped and they killed him too. The farmer happened to be passing and was wounded.

The sources said police suspected the attack was part of a campaign against suspected police collaborators by the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group). Minya province has been the centre of Gama'a activity for almost two years.

The Gama'a is the largest militant organisation fighting to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamic state. More than 1,000 people have been killed in political violence in Egypt since the group took up arms in 1992.
